answers.observation: The ball rolls continuously into contact, rebounds and continues under inertia; the result is not posed.
All three bottles begin responding at measured contact with continuous motion and no visible pose jump.
Two bottles remain horizontal while one returns upright; the asymmetric resting group looks solver-discovered.
Scale and seams read, but surface wear and convincing pebbled rubber remain too weak in the wide view.
The dark stippled shells read as opaque rough plastic, not glass, and different liquid levels are not reliably legible.
Boards, seams, line, baseboard, wall and bench establish human scale, although an exposed black boundary remains.
The cause image clearly establishes ball-to-bottle direction and distance without fitting the full support plane.
The contact clip changes from cause to contact camera at a timeline marker although its receipt claims a fixed contact camera; the still is two frames after first contact.
The effect frame is the measured end of the ten-frame settle window and all resting contacts remain solver-owned.
Physics clarity improves, but opaque bottles, the hidden clip camera cut, distant effect framing and black world edge prevent a materially believable improvement over RC3 H1.

reusableCorrectionsOnly: Use a clearer smooth transmissive glass response and brighter bounded bottle tints.
Add a perpendicular procedural court end wall and baseboard so semantic cameras cannot expose the world boundary.
Bind FIRST_CONTACT cinematography to the exact measured contact frame.
Fit SETTLED_GROUP_RESPONSE effect shots to the response targets rather than a distant initiator.
Remove timeline camera markers in the unsaved render-review process before rendering the claimed fixed-camera contact clip.
